about.title: Norco Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision upends everything, and in a community like Norco — where horse trails cross busy corridors like 6th Street and River Road — families are often left with questions no one seems ready to answer. Riverside County recorded traffic fatalities on Norco roads even in years with modest injury-collision counts, a reminder that any crash can turn catastrophic. California law gives a limited group of people, generally a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, and then other dependents or heirs, the right to bring a wrongful death claim. That claim is separate from any criminal charges the driver might face. We handle wrongful death matters directly and can walk you through your options, all on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.

items.title: Only Certain People Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, generally spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You'd Think
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity, like a public road authority, may be involved.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, as well as compensation for the loss of a loved one's companionship, guidance, and love.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Norco?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, which can come into play on corridors like I-15 or 6th Street, the deadline to act is much shorter, so it helps to talk with us soon.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this kind of claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a spouse or domestic partner and children as the first in line to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing, and we can clarify where your family fits.

items.question: Is this different from any criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the family, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed or how that case turns out. The two proceedings run independently of each other.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a consultation?
items.answer: No. We offer free consultations, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for your family.
